entries.subject: Lally et al. (2025) JWST MIRI + Spitzer 8 micron eclipse map (Eureka! reduction)
entries.finding: output_E.npy in Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.15103479 (MD5 dfb3f096bef955f228ed7e4d4bda12f0 as listed) holds fmap, tmap (12 x 24 cells), their uncertainties and the fitted times, fluxes and model. The paper's headline map is the Eureka! reduction, 2 eigenmaps at degree 5, hot spot 33.0 +0.7/-0.9 deg east. Hottest cell 1334.9 K at 37.5 E, 7.5 N; area-weighted dayside mean 1142 K. Turned by the package orbit and rotation it fits the 27,630 deposited MIRI samples with chi-squared 43,415, against 44,125 for a uniform planet and 45,783 for its east-west mirror.

entries.subject: Which longitudes the map shows
entries.finding: ThERESA (commit 74a8fec, utils.vislon and theresa.py) shows only cells overlapping the sub-observer longitude range widened by 90 degrees, and the authors' plotting script crops to it. From the times saved in output_E.npy and the configuration's t0 and period the range is -109.85 to 179.65 deg (the upper limit is ThERESA's wrapping of the Spitzer phase curve's limb); four columns, -180 to -120 deg, are not drawn.

entries.subject: The deposit's SPARTA-reduction map (output_S.npy)
entries.finding: The same fit on the SPARTA reduction of the MIRI data. It duplicates the Eureka! map's data and method; the paper leads with the Eureka! map.
entries.revisitWhen: The SPARTA and Eureka! maps are found to differ in a way the dataset should show.

entries.subject: This project's map from the raw MIRI exposures
entries.finding: packages/bake/src/objects/raster/eclipse-map/hd-189733b-raw-map.test.mts fits the two MIRI eclipses reduced from raw (JWST program 2021) and matches the deposited dayside with correlation 0.94, hot spot 41 E 7 N. It uses MIRI only, without the Spitzer data that break the ramp-map degeneracy, so it is a check, not a dataset.
entries.revisitWhen: A raw reduction adds the Spitzer data, or the program's remaining observations are mapped.

entries.subject: Earlier Spitzer 8 micron eclipse maps of HD 189733b
entries.finding: Lally et al. (2025) compare their map with earlier Spitzer eclipse maps and include the same Spitzer eclipses in their fit. Those maps were not searched for as data files in this change; the JWST map is shown as the most constrained.
entries.revisitWhen: An earlier map is found deposited as a data file and is worth comparing on the planet.

entries.subject: How far the hot spot moves with eclipse timing and light travel time
entries.finding: Measured in docs/eclipse-mapping.md: the eclipse-only map moves about 0.5-1 deg per second of timing; adding the 31 s of light travel time across the orbit, which ThERESA does not model, moves the offset from 42.3 to 26.4 deg in this project's fit. The paper's 33.0 deg lies inside that range. The map is shown as deposited.
entries.revisitWhen: A map of HD 189733b fitted with light travel time is published.

entries.subject: Time scale of the configuration's transit time
entries.finding: Lally et al. (2025) Table 1 labels t0 59838.6863112 UTC; the scene reads it as TDB. This project's TESS fit of HD 189733 puts the transit 6.4 +/- 0.9 s before that ephemeris, consistent with TDB and not with UTC, which would put it 69 s away. The difference is 0.1 percent of an orbit and the map is shown as fitted, so only the planet's displayed phase could move.

entries.subject: Which side of the star the planet crosses
entries.finding: An eclipse light curve cannot tell whether the planet crosses north or south of the star's centre; the orbit's construction fixes the map's north.
entries.revisitWhen: The orbit's sky orientation is measured.

entries.subject: Tidal locking of HD 189733b
entries.finding: Assumed, as in the paper's configuration (rotation period equal to the orbital period); not measured.
entries.revisitWhen: A rotation period of HD 189733b is measured.

entries.subject: Distant marker for HD 189733b
entries.finding: The deposited temperature map seen from the host star in the dataset palette, rendered by packages/telescope-cli/authoring/hd-189733/author.mts; --check recomputes it.

entries.subject: JWST eclipses of HD 189733b not in the shown map
entries.finding: MAST holds three eclipse visits the deposited map does not use: NIRCam F322W2 (GTO 1274, 26 Aug 2022, 5.8 h) and NIRCam F444W (GTO 1185, 28 Sep 2022, 6.1 h) at 2.4 to 5 microns, and a third MIRI eclipse in GO 2021 (24 Sep 2022, 4.7 h, phase 0.455 to 0.543) besides the two Lally et al. (2025) used. Whether they are good enough for a map is not checked.
entries.revisitWhen: A reduction of these visits from raw, or a published map that uses them.

entries.subject: NASA Eyes on Exoplanets artist's concept map as an illustration dataset
entries.finding: Shown as the non-default Illustration dataset, never as imagery: the map NASA's Eyes on Exoplanets app lists for HD 189733b (HD_189733_b.jpg), resized unchanged onto the sphere with its left edge at 0° longitude, so its longitudes are arbitrary. No image resolves this planet; nothing in the map was observed. NASA credits the app NASA/JPL-Caltech and calls each planet's look an artist's concept; the file itself carries no credit or date.

entries.subject: Uncertainty of the deposited MIRI brightness-temperature map
entries.finding: tmap_unc is the standard deviation of sampled temperature maps in ThERESA at 74a8fec, not total systematic uncertainty. The 12 x 24 cells range from 3.2717 to 9.5537 K; 240 visible cells keep exactly the thermal map grid and coverage. Prepared on a 0-10 K viridis scale. Timing, model choice and the deposit/paper run ambiguity remain outside this conditional spread.

entries.subject: HST/STIS reflected-light geometric albedo
entries.finding: Table 1 supplies six bins from 290 to 570 nm, their flux-weighted centres and asymmetric errors. All are plotted without interpolation, including the -0.11 fitted albedo. The two wider channels rebin the same eclipse, so they are not independent extra points. The uncovered 570-780 nm interval stays empty.

entries.subject: CHEOPS integrated geometric albedo
entries.finding: The thermally corrected geometric albedo is 0.076 +/- 0.016 in the 350-1100 nm CHEOPS band. It has a separate chart spanning the full passband, with no representative wavelength point or inferred spectral samples.

entries.subject: JWST NIRCam transmission spectrum and free-retrieval model
entries.finding: Zenodo 11459715 version 1 is CC BY 4.0. The exact deposited spectrum has 139 bins with overlapping filter coverage; depth and errors are multiplied by 100 for percentage. The deposited free-retrieval median file has 863 rows and 224 finite samples in the plotted range. No fit, rebinning or inter-filter shift is added. The published retrieval identifies H2O, CO2, CO and H2S; these are atmospheric interpretations, not spatial gas maps.

entries.subject: Observed visible-colour globe inferred from Hubble and CHEOPS albedos
entries.finding: The six Hubble bins stop at 570 nm; CHEOPS adds one overlapping broadband integral. They do not determine a full visible spectrum or an RGB surface map. The measurements are shown as charts, while NASA Illustration retains its artist-concept qualification.
entries.revisitWhen: A sufficiently sampled, calibrated visible reflectance spectrum and a justified colour-conversion method are available.
